# wget

Download files in scripts that run without a person. Use it to resume large downloads and to check that a URL answers.

## Rules

- **Use `-O` for a fixed output path.** Otherwise the file name comes from the URL.
- **Know that `-O` overwrites the file.** Choose a path that holds nothing you need.
- **Use `-c` to resume a download.** A retry then does not start again from zero.
- **Use `--spider` to check a URL only.** It downloads nothing.
- **Limit recursive options.** They can download far more than you need.
- **Do not assume curl or xh behaviour.** Redirects and authentication work differently in wget.

## Commands

```bash
wget -O output.bin https://example.com/file.bin
wget -c https://example.com/large-file.iso
wget --spider https://example.com/health
wget --tries=3 --timeout=20 https://example.com/archive.tgz
wget -qO- https://example.com/version.txt
```

## Output

- The `--spider` exit code shows whether the URL answers.
- Progress lines show the speed and the end of the transfer.
